biography: David Grusch previously worked in US Air Force and intelligence roles and was involved in government UAP reporting. In 2023 he became widely known after making allegations about programmes that he said were described to him by individuals with relevant access. His congressional statement describes his duties, his reporting to inspectors general and the constraints of discussing classified information publicly.

He appeared before the House Oversight subcommittee on 26 July 2023 alongside Ryan Graves and David Fravor. Grusch told lawmakers that he had been informed of alleged crash-retrieval and reverse-engineering activity. The publicly available statement documents that he made the allegations; it does not itself provide independently inspectable physical evidence for the programmes described.

His role in UAP disclosure debates is therefore different from that of a pilot describing a directly witnessed encounter. Researchers should distinguish first-person experience of intelligence reporting from second-hand descriptions of purported events, and review the original testimony rather than a chain of summaries.

biography: Retired Commander David Fravor commanded Strike Fighter Squadron 41 while serving with the USS Nimitz carrier group. His best-known UAP account concerns an encounter off the coast of California in November 2004 during a naval training period.

In his own written statement Fravor described being vectored towards an object by controllers on USS Princeton and observing a white, elongated object apparently moving over disturbed water. He recounted its motion, the efforts of his flight to observe it, and the circumstances in which the object was no longer visible. The account has featured prominently in later reporting on naval UAP encounters.

Fravor testified before a House Oversight subcommittee in July 2023. His firsthand account is a primary witness source, while claims about speed, distance and physical characteristics must still be evaluated alongside the quality and availability of sensor records, timings and independent observations. Video widely discussed alongside the incident should not be assumed to show the exact instant Fravor personally saw the object.

biography: Mick West is a writer, former video game developer and sceptical investigator who analyses unusual video, photography and claims using geometry, camera behaviour, environmental data and alternative explanations. He operates Metabunk, a public forum for investigating disputed material.

His UAP work has examined famous naval videos including Gimbal, GoFast and FLIR. In an analysis posted on Metabunk he argued that certain apparent rotations or movements can arise from sensor optics or viewing geometry, rather than directly revealing the physical movement of a craft. Such analyses are hypotheses to test against original data, not automatic identification of every object.

West's approach provides an important counterpoint to witness accounts and extraordinary interpretations. The most useful research comparison examines a specific observation, its source imagery, the assumptions in his reconstruction and the uncertainties that remain rather than treating scepticism or belief as a personal credibility score.

biography: Bob Lazar became a major figure in UAP popular culture in May 1989 when Las Vegas reporter George Knapp introduced an anonymous source on KLAS-TV who described alleged work at a secret site near Area 51. In subsequent appearances, Lazar spoke openly about the facility he called S-4 and claimed he had participated in attempts to understand unconventional propulsion systems. His television interviews are important original records of his testimony, regardless of whether the underlying story can be independently substantiated.

In his accounts Lazar described craft inside hangars, an element he referred to as 115, and a propulsion arrangement he said involved gravity. Reporters and researchers examined where he studied and what work he performed. Knapp told KNPR that some elements of Lazar's background were hard to verify; the same interview recounts reasons Knapp believed Lazar had been associated with Los Alamos. Neither this dispute nor the later scientific identification of element 115 by itself establishes an extraordinary propulsion technology.

The lasting research question is how to distinguish a claim made on camera, an independently documented biographical fact, and a physical assertion about equipment that outsiders have not been able to examine. Disclosure Desk treats the earliest KLAS appearances as source material and links to both contemporary footage and more critical journalistic assessments without giving an unsupported final verdict about Lazar's motives.

biography: Jake Barber is a US military veteran and helicopter pilot who became the subject of widespread UAP reporting in January 2025 after a NewsNation interview with Ross Coulthart. Barber described aviation and security work, including operations he said involved transporting objects of unusual appearance. NewsNation said it had examined documents that supported portions of his service background; those checks did not themselves demonstrate the existence of a non-human recovery programme.

In the broadcast Barber described lifting a smooth white egg-shaped object while piloting a helicopter with an external load. He also discussed a disc-shaped object with multiple sections, and claimed that some participants had interpreted the missions as connected with non-human intelligence. The programme displayed footage the broadcaster associated with the story. The recording's contents, custody, date, full context and object identification remain matters for careful investigation, separate from Barber's descriptions.

Barber's account is a useful case study for Evidence DNA because it combines an identified interviewee, unnamed alleged programme participants, portions of independently checked biography and a dramatic recording whose provenance is contested. A responsible comparison needs original, unedited media and logistics records before making assertions about a craft's composition or origin. The public interviews record what the participants claimed; they do not establish an extraordinary explanation.

biography: Steven M. Greer is a physician turned UFO/UAP disclosure advocate who founded and promoted the Disclosure Project. On 9 May 2001 he convened a National Press Club event in Washington, DC with speakers who described alleged UFO encounters, unusual programmes and government secrecy. Contemporary ABC News and UPI coverage documents the event and the group's call for formal congressional attention, while preserving the difference between the speakers' testimony and evidence verified outside the presentation.

Greer has also advocated a form of claimed human-initiated contact commonly called CE-5 and has produced books, films, witness presentations and additional press events. His own published materials describe these methods and his belief that some governments and corporations conceal advanced technology. Those positions are attributed to Greer and participating speakers, not statements confirmed by Disclosure Desk or by independent scientific testing.

His importance to the research history lies partly in organising and preserving large numbers of firsthand and secondhand accounts. The research challenge is to investigate each witness and document separately, distinguish independent testimony from shared source networks, and identify original observations or artefacts that could be assessed by outside investigators. An event with numerous speakers can be significant for public debate without settling the underlying physical claims.

biography: Larry Warren is a former US Air Force security specialist who has long spoken publicly about the December 1980 Rendlesham Forest events near the twin RAF Bentwaters and Woodbridge bases in Suffolk, England. With Peter Robbins he co-authored Left at East Gate, published in 1997, describing a further alleged encounter in which Warren said he was present. The book and later interviews became prominent in the wider Rendlesham story alongside better-documented accounts from other service personnel.

Important parts of Warren's personal narrative are contested. Other military participants, including Lt Col Charles Halt, have disputed his claimed presence or particular details of the incident; these criticisms are found in later interviews and case literature. Warren has continued to describe his experience in published discussions, including an interview with Steve LaPlume in 2023 and NewsNation coverage in 2025. A disagreement between witnesses should be examined at the level of specific claims, dates and original records, not treated as grounds for attacks on any person's character.

The UK National Archives preserves official correspondence and records concerning the reported Rendlesham incidents, including material associated with Halt. That material does not independently establish every later version of the event. For serious research, Warren's published account should be compared with contemporaneous military documents, the exact wording of different witnesses' statements, and the limitations of subsequent recollections. Disclosure Desk records the competing accounts without adopting a definitive personal credibility verdict.

biography: Luis Elizondo is a former US counterintelligence official who became a prominent public advocate for investigating UAP reports. The History Channel describes him as connected to the Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program. His own biography stresses disclosure and the need to treat unusual observations as a matter for investigation rather than dismissing witnesses.

He appeared in the History Channel's documentary series Unidentified: Inside America's UFO Investigation alongside Christopher Mellon and others. That programme follows investigations and interviews, mixing documentary material with interpretations supplied by participants; the programme itself is not independent proof of every anomaly discussed.

Elizondo published Imminent in August 2024 and has discussed his reported responsibilities and allegations in broadcast interviews and podcasts. Research should distinguish claims based on first-hand official roles, his later recollections and information attributed to other unnamed officials. Public statements are important historical sources but should not be treated as proof of a non-human explanation.

biography: Christopher Mellon served in senior US defence and intelligence roles, including as Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and a staff leader associated with Senate intelligence work. A public speaker biography documents this professional background and his later interest in UAP investigation.

Mellon appeared in the History documentary series Unidentified: Inside America's UFO Investigation alongside Luis Elizondo. His public writing and interviews have argued for a more coherent approach to collecting, analysing and publicly discussing unusual military aerial observations. He has also discussed the reporting of Navy UAP video and transparency debates.

The strongest research distinction is between his verifiable service and his analysis of what available government records imply. Policy advocacy, footage release and assertions about possible hidden programmes are separate kinds of evidence. His testimony and interviews provide valuable context but do not establish the physical identity or provenance of unidentified objects.

people.name: Avi Loeb
people.short: Harvard scientist seeking observational data on interstellar objects and UAP using instruments and testable hypotheses.
people.position: Loeb has argued that some unusual astronomical observations warrant open scientific investigation, and co-founded the Galileo Project in 2021.
people.context: A proposal to investigate a possible technological explanation is not evidence that extraterrestrial technology has already been identified; the project's reported measurements and methods require ordinary scientific scrutiny.
biography: Abraham (Avi) Loeb is an astrophysicist at Harvard University known for work on astrophysics and for openly discussing the possibility that unusual interstellar objects could have technological explanations. He has argued that scientific observations, rather than public fascination alone, should guide claims about unknown phenomena.

In July 2021 Loeb and Frank Laukien founded the Galileo Project. Harvard's project description states that it addresses both unidentified aerial phenomena and interstellar objects, with researchers pursuing instruments and analysis capable of generating new information. This is a scientific research programme; its existence does not demonstrate that any observation is of non-human origin.

Loeb has explored these questions in research articles, lectures and long-form podcasts. Disagreement with his interpretations should be approached by comparing physical measurements, model predictions and assumptions. His profiles are particularly useful to Disclosure Desk because Hypothesis Lab and Research Gap Finder are designed around this testable-evidence principle.

biography: Jacques Vallée is a computer scientist and author whose UFO research has extended across decades. He is known for investigating varied reports and for challenging the assumption that every anomalous experience can be explained by a single extraterrestrial-visitation hypothesis. His research work is documented on his own publications and media pages.

Vallée's film credits on his official media page include James Fox's The Phenomenon (2020) and the 2018 documentary Witness of Another World. His contributions include analysis of reports, cultural interpretation and discussion of evidence. Films record his contributions and those of other participants; the documentary format is not itself an independent verification.

Vallée has also participated in long-form interviews about his methods and archives, including a 2020 Joe Rogan appearance with filmmaker James Fox. Disclosure Desk can use those discussions as starting points for tracing sources, while maintaining separate labels for observational data, analytical theories and unconfirmed testimony.

biography: James Fox is a documentary filmmaker whose career in UFO and UAP reporting includes Out of the Blue, I Know What I Saw, The Phenomenon, Moment of Contact and The Program. Interviews with Fox describe his method of approaching witnesses and investigating controversial historical incidents.

His 2020 film The Phenomenon compiled historical material and interviews with officials and witnesses. Moment of Contact (2022) explored claims surrounding a 1996 incident in Varginha, Brazil, while The Program (2024) addressed government disclosure and congressional activity. These films are useful editorial syntheses, but do not substitute for independent examination of original interview recordings and physical evidence.

Fox has discussed his productions on podcasts including The Joe Rogan Experience, Astonishing Legends and Film School Radio. A useful Evidence DNA approach would link individual documentary statements to identified participants, dated versions and primary source records rather than treating repeated programme clips as separate confirmations.

people.name: Nick Pope
people.role: Former UK Ministry of Defence UFO desk officer (1965–2026)
people.short: Former UK civil servant known for handling UFO-related enquiries and later working as an author and broadcaster.
people.position: Pope served at the Ministry of Defence UFO desk from 1991 to 1994 and later contributed to books, podcasts and television documentaries.
people.context: His official memorial records that he died on 6 April 2026. Accounts of specific cases should be checked against released MoD records rather than treating later interviews as definitive investigation results.
biography: Nick Pope (1965–2026) was a British author and broadcaster who worked at the UK Ministry of Defence for 21 years. His official biographical memorial reports that he was assigned to the ministry's UFO desk between 1991 and 1994, where the role involved examining reports for defence significance and safety-of-flight concerns.

Pope wrote books about government UFO investigations and co-authored Encounter in Rendlesham Forest (2014) with witnesses John Burroughs and Jim Penniston. He later appeared in television programmes, documentary features and podcasts discussing UK cases such as Rendlesham and the 1993 Cosford wave. Documentary appearances record his commentary; the UK National Archives holds the original official government records that should be consulted alongside it.

His official website records his death on 6 April 2026, aged 60. Disclosure Desk preserves his public contributions as historical research rather than presenting him as a current spokesperson. His books, interviews and published recordings provide useful context, but particular conclusions about unexplained events remain subject to archival and scientific examination.
